items.stem: An AI ranks job applicants. Men score higher than equally skilled women. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: The AI chose to be unfair on purpose
options.B: The examples it learned from already favored men
options.C: The AI checked each résumé by hand

items.stem: "Biased data in, biased answers out" means:

options.A: Only bad people get bad AI
options.B: More data always removes unfair tilt
options.C: Unfair patterns in the examples show up in the outputs

items.stem: A face tool fails more often on darker skin. What should you check first?

options.A: Whether the practice examples covered many skin tones fairly
options.B: Whether the camera brand is expensive

items.stem: Why can an AI sound neutral and still treat groups differently?

options.B: It copies patterns from uneven examples, even without a written rule
options.C: It only fails when the power is low

items.stem: Your team wants a fairer hiring helper. Which step helps most?

options.C: Review the examples and test results across groups

items.stem: A chat tool gives weaker career advice to one gender. What does that show?

options.A: Uneven patterns in past text can shape the answers you see
options.B: The tool cannot write long sentences
options.C: Advice tools never need human review

items.stem: When is bias risk highest for a workplace AI?

options.A: Only when the screen is dark
options.B: When the examples leave out or undervalue some groups
options.C: Only when the AI uses rare words

items.stem: A map of "safe routes" avoids one district more than crime data supports. Likely reason?

options.C: Past reports or labels in the examples skewed that area

items.stem: You spot a tilted AI output at work. What is the best first move?

options.A: Pause, name the uneven pattern, and check the source examples or tests
options.B: Ship it faster so nobody notices
options.C: Assume the AI must be right because it sounds sure
